# 1 Enoch Chapter 30 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Watchers

---

**1** From there I traveled far to the east and came to another vast valley. There I saw the tree of judgment.

**2** Nearby stood large, beautifully fragrant trees called aloes — unlike any ordinary juniper trees.

**3** Past those valleys, continuing east to the farthest regions of the earth, I saw a great mountain covered in a forest of cedar, cypress, and sandalwood. Fragrant trees of the kind called Wanzeh also grew there, and cedar trees lined the slopes of the mountains on every side.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 30 continues the aromatic second journey. The "tree of judgment" (v. 1) is a striking, unexplained phrase — possibly the tree of knowledge near Eden's location. The forest of precious aromatic timbers (cedar, cypress, sandalwood, aloe, Wanzeh) represents the paradise-adjacent east of the ancient Near Eastern imagination. "Wanzeh" preserved as plant name.*
